messages:
ana_ml: Heads-up — bringing up morwen-7b (community release) on runtime v2.8. Seeing a weird token drift when we Q8 quantize + rotary KV. Repro steps below. Can someone triage?

liam_engineer: thx. can you paste the minimal repro and kernel/commit?

ana_ml: (oops typo) here's the exact run: 
```
MODEL=morwen-7b
RUNTIME=redwood-runtime:v2.8.3-rc
QUANT= q8_0  # PTQ via our offline tool
BATCH=1
SEQ=1024
python serve_client.py --model $MODEL --quant $QUANT --seq $SEQ --prompt-file samples/seed_prompts.txt
```
Output: after ~120 tokens the generated text starts repeating short phrases and losing coherence. Noticed KV cache sizes spike in logs right before drift.

devon_research: can you share a short example where it diverges? Also which rotary implementation? (rope vs rotary-mmap?)

ana_ml: example prompt id 7 from sample set. golden: "The committee concluded the findings were inconclusive and..." q8 output: "The committee concluded the findings were inconclusive and the the the the" — repeats. 
We use our rotary-mmap kernel (rotary-v2) and runtime picks kernel rot-mmap-archA.

liam_engineer: ok. two immediate suspects: 1) KV eviction/overflow with quantized KV entries, 2) rotary angle precision issue post-quant. Do we see any kernel warnings?

ana_ml: runtime logs show: 
```
WARN kv_cache: spill_count=0, entries=18432, entry_bytes=32768
WARN kernel_selector: selected rot-mmap-archA-q8 (fused);
ERROR attention: cached_rotary_scale mismatch: expected 1.0 got 0.999084
```

taylor_infra: hmm that 'cached_rotary_scale' mismatch stands out. sounds like float->int rounding in Q8 path. which quant library/scale table did you use?

ana_ml: used quant-tool v0.6 with per-channel scales exported. config attached in run: `scales_type: per_head` and we used the hermitian packing flag.

devon_research: can you run a non-quantized float32 run on same runtime (disable quant) but still use rot-mmap kernel? baseline seq perf and check whether rotary_scale mismatch is emitted.

ana_ml: running now, will paste shortly.

sre-bot: Scheduled ephemeral job: job/2309123456-morwen-f32-check queued on infra-pool-7. ETA ~ 2m.

liam_engineer: also try reducing SEQ to 128 to see whether eviction triggers matter. If drift disappears at short seq, that points to KV spill/evict.

ana_ml: f32 run logs: no 'cached_rotary_scale' error, output stays coherent to 512 tokens. So seems Q8 path triggers mismatch.

devon_research: can you dump the quant scales for a single attention head (head 2) and compare to runtime-used scale table? maybe serialization mismatch (endianness/ordering).

ana_ml: attaching short hex dump of scale[0..7] for head2: `0x3f800000 0x3f7a3d71 0x3f6f1cbc ...` Runtime prints `scale_table_head2[0]=0.987654` when parsed. They don't align.

taylor_infra: +1 on possible off-bytes. Also check pack/unpack flags between quant-tool and runtime (legacy pack vs new pack-v2). If runtime expects pack-v2 but quant-tool emitted legacy pack, indices shift and you get scale mismatch.

liam_engineer: mitigation plan: 1) block morwen q8 rollout, 2) add strict validation in onboarding to sanity-check scale tables post-load, 3) run a kernel-level unit test for cached_rotary_scale comparators.

devon_research: for immediate triage, can you try re-exporting quant with `--pack-version 2` and re-run? If that fixes the mismatch, it's config problem.

ana_ml: re-quant with pack-v2 in progress. if that fails i'll try q4_0 to see whether severity scales.

sre-bot: job/2309123456-morwen-requant-packv2 started on quant-host-3.ctl

liam_engineer: also add a small assert in runtime: if abs(cached_rotary_scale - expected) > 1e-3 then log full header dump and fallback to float path instead of continuing generation. That would avoid downstream hallucinated repeats in prod.

devon_research: agree. i'll open a quick PR with the assert + a unit test using a minimal packed scale file.

ana_ml: pack-v2 re-run looks promising — no rotary mismatch in initial 1024 tokens, coherence holds. thanks all. will follow up with the repro artifacts.

liam_engineer: great. please upload the failing binary quant artifact and the pack-v1 vs pack-v2 diffs to the onboarding ticket. we should also add a checklist item: "verify pack-version compatibility and scale-table parity" to the onboarding template.

ana_ml: noted — adding to intake checklist. :white_check_mark:
